outcome-unread.why: the run wrote no readable outcome file: it crashed or was cut off, which says nothing about the issue

outcome-invalid.why: the run's outcome file names no known exit, a fault in the run, not a finding about the issue

scan-refused-patch.why: the scan job refused the run's patch for its size, and the run job's scan of it found no credential shape or binary hunk, so a fresh run may make a smaller one

scan-refused-fault.why: the scan job could not finish, or a patch with no binary hunk, its added text scanned, did not apply to the head: a job fault that says nothing about a credential, so a fresh run scans again

scan-refused-output.why: the scan job refused the run's output for a reason only its log names, which may be a credential shape, or a patch it could not prove clear of one, a security judgment

collect-refused.why: the patch collector refused a file the run left at a stub name such as .npmrc or .env, which may be a planted credential or config file, a security judgment

issue-file.why: the runner could not write the issue file, a runner fault before any model ran

issue-edited.why: the issue's title or body changed after agent-ready was added, and only a listed human's new agent-ready admits the edited text

patch-protected-path.why: the change needs a path the issue lane may not push, which a maintainer session builds by hand

host-only.why: the run reports the work needs a host run the lane cannot make

manual-external.why: the run reports the work needs a manual step on external state, one of pr-pipeline.yaml's attended classes, which needs the owner present

patch-credential.why: apply-issue-patch refused the patch because it or a file it writes carries a credential shape, a token-leak path the owner keeps a hold on

patch-invalid.why: apply-issue-patch refused the patch as missing, too large or made on another commit, a fault in the run's output, so a fresh run makes it again

patch-not-applied.why: the patch did not apply to the commit the run started from, so a fresh run starts from the current one

patch-apply-failed.why: apply-issue-patch failed before it committed or refused the patch, a job fault

done-no-commit.why: the run reported done but committed nothing

resumed-unchecked.why: the runner's checks did not pass over the resumed branch, so the next run continues it

check-failed.why: a check the runner ran on the branch failed or could not be read, so the next run continues the branch

required-undone.why: the run left a required check undone, so the next run continues the branch

hold-label-failed.why: the held PR could not be labeled human-merge-hold, a failed write, not a finding about the issue

pr-head-moved.why: the PR opened at a head other than the tip the runner checked, a race, not a finding about the issue

closed-by-open-pr.why: an open PR the lanes App or a listed human opened already closes the issue, a race with the earlier-work check, not a finding about the issue; while it stays open the next run stops before any model turn

turn-cap-spent.why: the run reached its turn cap with no restart left

retry-spent.why: the lane has retried this issue as many times as limits.stop-retries, or the stop's own row, allows

pushback.why: the run names cause intent: the issue leaves its intended outcome open, an intent question only a person answers

pushback-means.why: the run pushed back without naming cause intent, so its question is a choice of means or a design detail, and intake triage decides it again on evidence and admits it, unless its own intent, security or cost rules stop it

intent-change.why: the run found the work changes the issue's intent, which a person decides

design-change.why: the run found the work changes the primary design, which a person decides

security-risk.why: the run reports a HIGH or CRITICAL security risk, which a person decides

cost-risk.why: the run reports a HIGH or CRITICAL cost risk, which a person decides

stopped.why: the run stopped for a reason it gave no code for, which names no intent, design, security or cost finding, so the lane runs it again only if the issue has had no retry, for any stop, since a listed human last added agent-ready, and otherwise stops

split-required.why: the issue's Size is too large for one run, and intake's split (owner Q93) files its sub-issues

research-first.why: the issue's Uncertainty says research comes first, a step no person decides, so it parks as admission parks the same refusal

probe-first.why: the issue's Uncertainty says only an experiment answers it, a step no person decides, so it parks as admission parks the same refusal

blocked-by-pr.why: the work waits on an open pull request the run names, so the lane runs it again once that pull request merges or closes

already-done.why: the run found the issue's work already on the default branch at a commit it cites, so the issue closes

report-delivered.why: the issue asks for a report and no change, and the run posted that report, so the issue closes
